title: TrustDomain string form is not injective: distinct trust domains collide after a URI round-trip
description:
hire-core/src/spiffe_id.rs:51-62 (Display) and :143-157 (parse_trust_domain). Display is many-to-one against the parser, so `SpiffeId::from_str(&id.uri())` can return a different trust domain than the one you started with:

- `TrustDomain::OrgOidc("tailscale".into())` displays as `tailscale`, parses back as `TrustDomain::Tailscale` (spiffe_id.rs:145).
- `TrustDomain::OrgOidc("personal.example".into())` displays as `personal.example`, parses back as `TrustDomain::PersonalDid("example")` (spiffe_id.rs:149-150).
- Same for any OIDC issuer domain beginning `piv.` or equal to `ssh.local` / `pgp.local`.

The domain string is attacker-influenced in the one place it is built from external input: hire-attestors/src/oidc.rs:81-88 takes the `iss` claim out of a cached JWT, strips the scheme (oidc.rs:45-51) and wraps it in `OrgOidc` with no validation. An issuer of `https://piv.acme.example` yields a SPIFFE ID that anyone re-parsing reads as a PIV smart-card trust domain — a different, higher-trust source. The collision matters because the URI, not the serde form, is what goes into the SVID subject (signer.rs:103) and into the trust-bundle key (trust_bundle.rs:47).

Related gap in the same area: `parse_trust_domain` is a private free function (spiffe_id.rs:143) and there is no `impl FromStr for TrustDomain`, so a caller holding a trust-domain string — the exact thing `TrustBundleStore::get(&str)` and the FetchJWTBundles map keys hand back — cannot turn it into a `TrustDomain` at all.

Also note `parse_trust_domain` is total: `SpiffeIdError::MissingTrustDomain` (spiffe_id.rs:17-18) is only ever produced for the empty string (spiffe_id.rs:127), never for a malformed domain, so `SpiffeId: FromStr` accepts any non-empty authority.

Pre-1.0 options: reserve a prefix namespace per variant (`oidc.` for OrgOidc) so Display is injective, or make TrustDomain hold a validated single string plus a kind tag, or make parsing fallible and reject ambiguous authorities.
close_reason: Fixed in f74bd20. Every TrustDomain variant now owns a reserved authority (oidc.{domain} is the new one), so Display is injective and parse is its exact inverse. An authority in no reserved namespace does not parse, which is the constraint rather than a gap -- hired holds no bundle for a domain it did not mint. TrustDomain gained the public FromStr the bead asked for, and authorities are checked against the SPIFFE character set before the namespace match so malformed reads as malformed rather than unknown. Case-folding deliberately not done: it would make OIDC.example.com a second spelling and break injectivity through the back door. The pseudonym known-answer vector moved with the salt and was recomputed by re-running the documented python HKDF command, not by copying the code's output. SPEC-HIRE's trust domain table and example URIs updated.
